title: Experience profile

domain.defaultBehavior: baseline identity; a selection composes closed per-axis postures whose expansion always loses to any authored field or channel

compatibility: closed versioned registry (expressive-profiles); ids permanent, superseded by @N+1; unset-to-rollback

normalizedStops.law: profile-id: the tenant writes this opaque registry ID verbatim; there is no normalized NUMBER for a profile stop, so `value` is null by contract rather than 0 (which would read as a bounded stop at zero). Axes: geometry sharp, edge hairline, material flat, elevation hairline-lift, motif none, density normal, motion unset.

profile-id: written verbatim, as above. Axes: geometry soft, edge ruled, material paper, elevation soft-depth, motif contour, density spacious, motion {intensity 0.7, durationScale 1.1, ambient subtle} — the motion field default is why `motion remains fixed` is NOT declared control-wide (see negativeControlsScopeNote).

calibration.nextAction: OBTAIN_SIGHTED_ACCEPTANCE. OPEN_ARM_ASYMMETRY closes with the new law rather than with an exception: the asymmetry it named was real and is now removed in the decidable scopes, measured rather than argued. The dark residual is OPEN_VERTICAL_CASCADE_DEFECT's, and the owner's simplification question is unrelated to it.
calibration.catalogLaw: catalogo en calibration, NO en enumValues: cerrado por REGISTRO first-party versionado (crece por registro, no por schema); ids permanentes, superseded por @N+1
calibration.negativeControlsScopeNote: Only `color remains fixed` is declared, and that is a deliberate floor rather than an omission. `font metrics remain fixed` must NEVER be declared here: --ds-letter-spacing-heading is one of this control's own five declared channels and is the packet's primary painted witness, so that entry would report the control's intended effect as a violation. `border remains fixed` and `border width and style remain fixed` are excluded for the same class of reason: the edge axis owns --ds-edge-standard-width and the geometry axis moves radiusScale as a FIELD DEFAULT, so both entries would fence the control against itself. `motion remains fixed` is excluded because it is TRUE PER STOP, not control-wide: management-editorial sets {intensity 0.7, durationScale 1.1, ambient subtle} as a field default, so a control-wide declaration would be a false claim about the control even though no motion channel is carried in the declared five-channel payload. `control height remains fixed` is bound to control-bearing targets and the only bindable target here is a Card root, which is not one.

measuredResult.scenarios: 4 receipted positives = {rottay,evnto} x {technical,editorial}, both ingress doors on ONE scene, both themes. All four self-check harness-live; ingressEquivalence identical with 0 differing rows; restore.exact true and negativeControls.held true on every arm of every scenario. Two further scenarios were measured and deliberately NOT receipted: bithire/technical (DESIGNED_NULL) and bithire/editorial (DIVERGENCE) - see knownDefects.
measuredResult.directChannel: token-readout reads all five declared channels directly and is therefore the direct-read control fixture (directControlFixtureIds requires ONE target to read EVERY declared channel). --ds-letter-spacing-heading moved on both arms in all four scenarios: rottay -0.015em -> 0.01em (technical) and -> 0 (editorial); evnto likewise from its own baseline.
measuredResult.paintedDelta: card-modern-md/title letter-spacing, identical on both arms, in BOTH themes, in all four receipted scenarios: rottay -0.196875px -> 0.13125px (technical) and -> normal (editorial); evnto -0.3px -> 0.15px (technical) and -> normal (editorial). That is 8 painted cells. card-modern-md/root background-image also moves via --ds-elevation-lift-strength, but ASYMMETRICALLY BY THEME: the editorial stop (lift 2) moves it in both themes, while the technical stop (lift 0) moves it in DARK ONLY, because light themes already resolve the lift to 0 and the stop is then a true no-op for that axis.
measuredResult.chain: letter-spacing: var(--ds-card-title-letter-spacing, var(--ds-letter-spacing-heading)) at .ds-card--modern > body > header > header-main > title (card.css:521). The title part had to be added to the card-modern-md fixture for this packet; it is rendered by the REAL ModernCard, so the roster drift test covers it.
measuredResult.titleWitnessNote: The editorial stop drives letter-spacing to the INITIAL value (normal) because --ds-letter-spacing-heading: 0 is substituted unitless and is invalid at computed-value time. The movement is real and reversible; it is the unhydrated guard that cannot decide such a target from its longhands alone, which is why both measured targets carry border-top-style as a hydration witness.
measuredResult.supersededStatus: MEASURED UNDER THE PRE-H-1 INSTRUMENT. Every number in this object is preserved verbatim as historical evidence and is a faithful record of that run. What no longer holds is the CONCLUSION drawn from it: the static arm was compiling a one-field theme, so the static half of "ingressEquivalence identical with 0 differing rows" describes a scene production does not ship. knownDefects.finding: REFUTED BY RE-MEASUREMENT UNDER THE CORRECTED INSTRUMENT (H-1, 2026-08-23). This control was closed COMPUTED_VERIFIED on 4 receipts measured while the static ingress arm compiled a ONE-FIELD BrandTheme -- the stop alone, with no vertical baseline. H-1 made that arm compose the stop over the vertical's published theme, which is what production ships, and the same 6 painted cases were re-run: in ALL SIX the static arm is INERT for --ds-letter-spacing-heading (moved:false) while the DB arm moves it (rottay -0.015em -> 0.01em technical / -> 0 editorial; evnto -0.02em -> 0.01em / -> 0; bithire -0.01em -> 0.01em / -> 0). ingressEquivalence is false in all six, so none of the four scenarios re-validates as a positive evidence kind. The receipts are NOT withdrawn and their numbers are NOT rewritten: they are a faithful record of what the pre-H-1 instrument measured, kept as historical evidence. What is withdrawn is the COMPUTED_VERIFIED claim resting on them. ROOT CAUSE, MEASURED, AND IT IS TWO DIFFERENT CAUSES. (a) rottay and evnto: the composed static arm emits EXACTLY the value the vertical's artifact already authors (rottay -0.015em at artifacts/rottay/index.css:631, evnto -0.02em at artifacts/evnto/index.css:257), because the profile loses to the authored field INSIDE compileBrandTheme -- the precedence the compiler itself declares (brand-theme/index.ts:758-773, authored > profile > seeds). The arm writes the value that was already there, so nothing moves. This is production-true, not an instrument defect. (b) bithire: its artifact declares the channel TWICE (:644 -0.025em and :1496 -0.01em in the higher-specificity dark block); the arm emits -0.025em and loses to the dark block. That is OPEN_VERTICAL_CASCADE_DEFECT, orthogonal, and still open.
knownDefects.remediation: CLOSED for every scope this instrument can decide, by B-1 (owner option B). The product question this defect was waiting on -- may a profile selection move a channel the vertical authors -- was answered by the owner: the tenant prevails over the vertical baseline on exposed channels, technical and accessibility invariants protected. Cause (a) rottay/evnto is resolved: the static transport now has the two-floor ingestion, so the profile no longer loses to the vertical's authored field when the selection comes from the tenant. Cause (b) bithire dark is NOT this control's and is tracked as OPEN_VERTICAL_CASCADE_DEFECT. The pre-H-1 receipts are still not withdrawn and their numbers still not rewritten; the six R7 artifacts are additional evidence beside them, under new file names, never overwriting the historical record.

knownDefects.finding: On bithire and in DARK ONLY, the STATIC ingress door cannot move --ds-letter-spacing-heading while the DB door can. bithire's compiled artifact declares the channel twice: at base tenant specificity (artifacts/bithire/index.css:644, -0.025em) and again in a dark block whose selector carries an EXTRA attribute/class - :is(html[data-tenant='bithire'], :where([data-ds-root][data-vertical='bithire']))[data-theme='dark'], ....dark (line 1496, -0.01em). The static arm lands behind the BASE selector, so the dark block outranks it; the DB arm writes inline on documentElement and outranks everything. Reproduced twice, identical rows. knownDefects.finding: On bithire/editorial and in LIGHT, --ds-material-canvas-texture moves on the STATIC arm and not on the DB arm. Distinct cause from the row above: compileTenantThemeConfig emits only 3 of the 5 declared channels for bithire/editorial (--ds-edge-standard-width and --ds-material-canvas-texture are absent), because the profile expansion loses to a channel the vertical baseline already authors - the control's own declared defaultBehavior. The static lowering has no vertical baseline to lose to, so it emits.
knownDefects.boundedBy: The asymmetry is bounded to channels a vertical authors. rottay and evnto author neither channel and both arms agree there, which is why their four scenarios are byte-identical across doors.
knownDefects.remediation: Owner adjudication: decide whether the static door should also lose to an authored vertical channel (making the doors symmetric) or whether the DB door should stop losing (making the control uniformly stronger). Either way it is a compiler decision above this packet.

knownDefects.finding: bithire x rottay/bithire-technical@1 is a STRUCTURAL IDENTITY, not a calibration cell: brand-themes/bithire/index.ts:3190 already declares experienceProfile 'rottay/bithire-technical@1', so a bithire tenant selecting that stop selects the profile the vertical already has. It is measured and retained as evidence, deliberately NOT receipted, and must not be read as an inert-control finding.

calibration.armEquivalenceCriterion: THE OPERATIONALISATION OF THE OWNER'S "static and DB must produce exactly the same result", written before it was measured (Z-2). Equality is of COMPUTED VALUES over the real cascade, never of emitted-map size: the static arm emits a COMPLETE compiled theme while the DB arm emits a tenant-scoped DELTA that overlays the vertical's base CSS, so the two are different KINDS of output and a map-size or key-set comparison is a category error. Measured: 52 variables on the DB arm against 1231 on the static arm for the same tenant and profile, with --ds-color-primary absent from the DB map entirely. The comparison is therefore: for every declared channel the DB arm emits, the value it emits must equal the value the static arm emits; a channel the DB arm does not emit is resolved by the cascade to the vertical base, which the static arm already carries, so it cannot disagree. Reading the DB delta as if it were a whole theme is the false-red this criterion exists to prevent, and comparing only the intersection without saying so is the false-green.
calibration.armEquivalenceResult: 6/6 painted cases equivalent at --theme light, ZERO differing rows, selfCheck harness-live, per-vertical source digests declared (a single digest reused across verticals trips the stale-source guard, because each vertical's compiled artifact is in its own freshness surface). The static arm MOVES --ds-letter-spacing-heading on 3/3 verticals where H-1 measured it inert on 6/6, and both arms land on the pairing vocabulary. At the variable level, 22/22 channel readings agree. The two surviving rows are BOTH dark-scope letter-spacing on bithire, and they are ledgered against OPEN_VERTICAL_CASCADE_DEFECT -- a packet of the vertical generator/cascade, not of this control. Its cause is written and measured: bithire's artifact declares the channel TWICE (src/foundation/tokens/css/facade/artifacts/bithire/index.css:644 '-0.025em' and :1496 '-0.01em' inside the higher-specificity dark block). Compounding it, the probe never applies compiled MODE BLOCKS -- the string 'modeBlocks' appears nowhere in src/tooling/resolution-probe -- so a dark-scope reading measures the shipped artifact CSS rather than the compile. The compile is correct there and was measured: with a tenant floor bithire's base emits --ds-letter-spacing-heading '0' and the dark block emits NOTHING, so dark inherits the tenant value; without one, base emits '-0.025em' and dark restates '-0.01em'. Dark is therefore measured-and-NOT-receipted (bithire-editorial.RESIDUAL-DARK-SCOPE.json), never claimed as parity.
